messages:
Priya Nair: Heads-up: support ticket — quickstart README uses REDWOOD_API_TOKEN but our Python SDK reads REDWOOD_API_KEY. New users got a silent 401 then abandoned the tutorial.

Tom Briggs: Yikes. Paste the snippet?

Priya Nair: Current README snippet:
```py
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_TOKEN'))
```

Priya Nair: Should be:
```py
import os
from redwood import create_client
client = create_client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
```

Maya Chen: Two problems: env var mismatch and old blocking client in example. create_client wires our recommended retry/backoff and surfaces clearer 401 messaging.

Tom Briggs: Fix plan?

Priya Nair: 1) Update README to use REDWOOD_API_KEY and create_client; 2) add one-line FAQ about 401s caused by wrong env var; 3) add CI smoke: run python quickstart with a fake token and assert error suggests checking REDWOOD_API_KEY; 4) add onboarding checklist note for SE demos. I'll open the PR.

doc-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/814 "python quickstart: env var + create_client + retry note"

Maya Chen: Nice. Make the PR include a tiny test so this regresses loudly if docs drift again. Also add a short note in the SDK changelog referencing the export/name change so integrators scanning releases see it.

Priya Nair: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1120  CI running.

doc-bot: CI started for docs/pr-1120  lint + smoke tests.

Tom Briggs: Thanks Priya! Once merged I'll update the internal demo checklist.

Priya Nair: Merged  CI green. Closing the loop.
